vulnerabilities.weakness: Stateful cache with no persistent volume and single replica, no PDB or HPA, can lose cart data and halt checkout
vulnerabilities.hypothesis: if the redis-cart pod is killed, the cartservice will be unable to read or write cart data, causing checkout to fail

vulnerabilities.weakness: Single replica, entrypoint, no PDB/HPA; pod loss brings down entire site
vulnerabilities.hypothesis: if the frontend pod is killed, all user-facing traffic is lost, causing site outage

vulnerabilities.weakness: Single replica, no PDB/HPA, depends on redis-cart; pod loss stalls checkout
vulnerabilities.hypothesis: if the cartservice pod is killed, checkoutservice will timeout waiting for cart data, slowing or breaking checkout

vulnerabilities.weakness: Single replica, no PDB/HPA, on checkout path; pod loss degrades product lookup
vulnerabilities.hypothesis: if the productcatalogservice pod is killed, checkoutservice will fail to retrieve product info, slowing checkout

vulnerabilities.weakness: Single replica, no PDB/HPA, on checkout path; pod loss delays currency conversion
vulnerabilities.hypothesis: if the currencyservice pod is killed, checkoutservice will wait for conversion, slowing checkout

vulnerabilities.weakness: Single replica, no PDB/HPA; pod loss only affects email notifications, expected to fail gracefully
vulnerabilities.hypothesis: if the emailservice pod is killed, checkoutservice will skip sending confirmation emails but still complete checkout

vulnerabilities.weakness: Single replica, no PDB/HPA; pod loss may delay payment processing but checkout can retry
vulnerabilities.hypothesis: if the paymentservice pod is killed, checkoutservice will retry payment calls and eventually succeed

vulnerabilities.weakness: Single replica, no PDB/HPA; pod loss delays shipping estimate but checkout can proceed
vulnerabilities.hypothesis: if the shippingservice pod is killed, checkoutservice will use default shipping estimate and continue checkout

systemic: All services run a single replica with no PDB or HPA, exposing the entire stack to single‑point failures and lack of autoscaling
blind_spots: Facts do not reveal internal timeout, retry, or circuit‑breaker logic; cannot assess how services recover from transient network or CPU spikes
